_comment: File paths both runtimes' flight recorders must agree to exclude. Read by python/tests/test_excluded_path_parity.py and typescript/src/flight-recorder/excluded-path-parity.test.ts, so a pattern added to one runtime cannot silently miss the other.
_why_it_matters: Exclusion is not about hiding the path -- a path is not a secret. When a recorded object carries a file locator for an excluded path, every sibling field in that object is replaced with [excluded-path], including `content`. The only survivors are the short file-metadata allowlist below. So a credential file missing from this list means its CONTENTS are written to the flight log. Value-pattern matching rescues contents that happen to look like a known credential shape, but it is unreliable: a .pgpass line and an .npmrc auth token both reached the log verbatim before these entries existed.
_safe_metadata_comment: The blanking sweep has one deliberate hole: these fields describe the file rather than reveal it, so they survive next to an excluded locator. Any field NOT named here is blanked. `numeric` fields survive only for a finite, non-negative, non-boolean number; `text` fields only for a string that survives sanitization unchanged and fits maxTextBytes. Measure that budget in UTF-8 BYTES, not in whatever a runtime calls a string's length: Python's len() counts code points and JavaScript's .length counts UTF-16 code units, so a 200-emoji `mime` value is 200 to one runtime and 400 to the other, and the two disagree about whether it rides along next to a credential path. Every other size cap in the flight recorder is already measured in UTF-8 bytes.
_depth_guard_comment: Deciding whether a value hides an excluded file locator means walking it. The walk stops at maxTraversalDepth and then fails closed, treating anything deeper as if it did hide one. That guard is only meaningful for containers: a value that is not a mapping or a sequence has no keys, so whether it hides a locator is answerable exactly, at any depth, without walking anything. Deciding non-containers before the depth guard rather than after is what keeps the answer from depending on the type of the leaf -- otherwise two structures of identical shape are classified differently because one ends in a string and the other in a number.
_must_keep_comment: Over-exclusion is worse here than in key redaction: a single false positive blanks every sibling field in the object, so an ordinary file can destroy a whole record. Public keys are the sharp case -- a PUBLIC key is not a secret, and the trailing anchor in the id_* pattern is what keeps `id_rsa.pub` readable. Note that anything under ~/.ssh is excluded wholesale by the directory rule, deliberately and regardless of name, so the .pub cases below are deliberately outside it.
